evals.prompt: Rebase fix/a and feat/b onto origin/develop. First build the scratch repository with `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>` (setup-scratch.sh is the fixture; the clone to work in is <empty-dir>/work and its remote is the local bare repository <empty-dir>/origin.git). Do not push anything yet.
evals.expected_output: The batch is established and pinned, with backups and records, before any branch moves.
expectations: The rebase skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent reads the repository instructions (AGENTS.md) and inspects git status, git worktree list, remotes, and each branch's upstream before changing anything
Both branches are resolved to local refs/heads names, and fix/a and feat/b are found to be not checked out, so each is rebased in a new linked worktree outside the main checkout
The target and each upstream are fetched, and one target pin commit ID is captured and shared by both branches, along with each branch's start and lease
A backup ref refs/rebase-backup/<name> exists for each branch, created with git update-ref at the start commit
A batch directory outside every checkout holds one record file per branch with the fields location, start, lease, old merge base, phase, new tip, check results, push result

evals.prompt: Use the rebase skill to rebase fix/a onto origin/develop in the scratch repository built by `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>` (clone at <empty-dir>/work). fix/a and develop both changed TIMEOUT_SECONDS in settings.py. Do not push. If a conflict needs a product decision, my answer is to keep develop's 45 seconds (the gateway limit) and note the trade-off.
evals.expected_output: The conflict is resolved by intent through resolve-merge-conflicts, continued with git rebase --continue, and validated.
expectations: The rebase is run on the pinned target with GIT_EDITOR=true and with rebase.updateRefs=false overridden, and no autostash
When Git stops on the conflict, the resolve-merge-conflicts skill is called with the target pin as the goal

The resolution cites the intent of both commits (OPS-31 raise to 60 seconds for slow exports, OPS-28 set 45 seconds to match the gateway limit), stops to ask first because the intent is incompatible, and then keeps 45 as the user decided, recording the trade-off
The agent stages only the reviewed conflict path and runs git rebase --continue, so the original commit message and order are kept, instead of making a new commit
Git reports no unfinished rebase and no unmerged entries after the last commit
The new tip is validated: the target pin is an ancestor, git range-diff is reviewed and each changed patch explained, make check passes, and git diff --check passes

evals.prompt: Use the rebase skill on fix/a and feat/b onto origin/develop in the scratch repository built by `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>` (clone at <empty-dir>/work). When both are rebased and validated, give me your report and wait. I haven't decided what to push. If a conflict needs a product decision, my answer is to keep develop's 45 seconds (the gateway limit) and note the trade-off.
evals.expected_output: One report table and an explicit question about which branches to push, with no push yet.
expectations: One table shows for each branch the start, new tip, conflicts and their key decisions, check results, push destination, and status

The report includes the target pin, the batch directory, and the undo command per branch (git reset --keep refs/rebase-backup/<name> in its checkout, or git branch -f <name> refs/rebase-backup/<name> when it is not checked out)
The agent then asks which branches to push and offers only rebased and validated branches that have a destination
No git push has been run when the turn ends

evals.prompt: Use the rebase skill on feat/b onto origin/develop in the scratch repository built by `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>` (clone at <empty-dir>/work, remote <empty-dir>/origin.git). After the report I approve pushing feat/b to origin.
evals.expected_output: A guarded push with an explicit lease, verified by reading the remote back, and cleanup of what the skill created.
expectations: Before pushing, the agent confirms the local branch still equals its validated tip
The push uses --force-with-lease with the explicit form refs/heads/feat/b:<lease commit ID> captured before the rebase, with push.followTags=false and --recurse-submodules=no, and never plain --force
After the push the remote is read with git ls-remote --refs and the branch is marked pushed and verified only because the remote tip equals the new tip
The worktree the skill created is removed with git worktree remove
The agent offers to delete the refs/rebase-backup refs and keeps them unless the user agrees

evals.prompt: Use the rebase skill on feat/b onto origin/develop. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>`, then from a second clone of <empty-dir>/origin.git commit a new file `extra.txt` on feat/b and push it, so origin/feat/b has a commit the local feat/b lacks. Work in <empty-dir>/work.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks before rebasing because pushing the branch would delete the remote commit.
expectations: After fetching, the agent finds that local feat/b is behind origin/feat/b
The agent asks whether to bring the remote commits in first, and explains that pushing without them would delete them from the remote
The agent does not rebase feat/b before the answer, and records the answer once given

evals.prompt: Use the rebase skill on fix/a and feat/b onto origin/develop. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>`, then in <empty-dir>/work run `git checkout fix/a` and append a line to notes.txt without committing. Work in <empty-dir>/work. If asked what to do with the uncommitted edit, my answer is to skip fix/a and carry on with feat/b.
evals.expected_output: The user's uncommitted work is left alone and the agent asks what to do with it.
expectations: The agent detects that fix/a is checked out in a checkout with uncommitted work
The agent asks whether to commit, stash, or skip that branch, and does not stash, reset, or discard the edit itself
feat/b, which is not checked out, is still handled in its own linked worktree

evals.prompt: Use the rebase skill on feat/b onto origin/develop. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>`, then add a file test_gateway.py with a test that always fails to develop in <empty-dir>/work, commit it, and push develop to origin, so `make check` fails on the target. Work in <empty-dir>/work. Report only.
evals.expected_output: The failing check is traced to its origin but stays a failure; only the user can waive it.
expectations: make check fails on the new tip, and the branch is marked rebased, checks failing rather than rebased and validated
The agent checks whether the failure already exists at the branch start or at the target pin using a separate worktree, and records the evidence that it comes from the target
The report still shows the failure as a failure, and the push offer includes feat/b only on the condition that the user explicitly waives the named failing check

evals.prompt: Use the rebase skill on fix/a and feat/c onto origin/develop. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>`, then in <empty-dir>/work create feat/c on top of fix/a with one extra commit, so feat/c sits on top of fix/a. Work in <empty-dir>/work. If asked whether they are a stack, my answer is yes. If a conflict needs a product decision, my answer is to keep develop's 45 seconds (the gateway limit) and note the trade-off.
evals.expected_output: The stack is detected and asked about, then rebased as one unit from its top.
expectations: The agent notices that feat/c sits on top of fix/a and asks whether to treat them as a stack
Once confirmed, the stack is rebased as one unit from its top (feat/c) with --update-refs instead of overriding rebase.updateRefs=false
Both branches end up on the new target, each with its own backup ref and record
Each branch in the stack is validated and reported separately

evals.prompt: Use the rebase skill to resume. A batch directory exists from an earlier session in the scratch repository: it holds records for fix/a (phase 'validated', new tip recorded, checks passed) and feat/b (phase 'rebasing', start recorded, no new tip). The earlier session crashed, and meanwhile the target has advanced by one commit. A subagent may still have been working on feat/b's worktree.
evals.expected_output: The batch is resumed from its records with the original pins, and branches whose state cannot be established are asked about.
expectations: The agent reads RESUME.md and the batch directory before touching any branch
The agent keeps the recorded target pin, starts, leases and answers as its default and does not re-pin to the advanced target on its own; it may mention that the target advanced
The agent establishes through the host's actual execution state that no earlier subagent can still change feat/b's checkout, and marks the branch unknown and asks when it cannot
fix/a is kept as validated when its local tip equals the recorded validated tip, without redoing the rebase
The agent's report or stop message accounts for every branch of the batch, fix/a as validated and feat/b as unknown

evals.prompt: I'm in the middle of rebasing my branch by hand and Git stopped with a conflict in settings.py. The branch is already the one I chose and I only need the conflict sorted out and the rebase finished.
evals.expected_output: An already-running operation stopped on a conflict is resolve-merge-conflicts, not a new batch rebase.
expectations: The rebase skill is not invoked: no batch, target pin, backup ref, or push is set up
The agent resolves the in-progress conflict with the resolve-merge-conflicts skill and continues the existing rebase

evals.prompt: My worktree branch worktree/csv-export is finished and committed. Bring it back into the main checkout's branch.
evals.expected_output: Landing a worktree branch back to the original checkout is sync-tree.
expectations: The rebase skill is not invoked and no history is rewritten
The request is handled by the sync-tree skill, a transfer of committed history to the corresponding local branch
